prompt: Unseen regulated workload: produce a provider-neutral cloud design, translate it accurately to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, then diagnose changed zone, quota, policy, control-plane, managed-data and cost constraints without creating cloud resources.
deliverables: User operations, SLI/SLO, data classification, residency, RPO and RTO contract.
Governance hierarchy, environment isolation, identity, policy inheritance, billing and audit map.
Data path and control path with exact state scopes and owners.
Provider-neutral compute, network, data, elasticity, observability and recovery design.
Failure-domain table covering instance, zone, region, control plane and shared dependencies.
Capacity, quota, rate, startup, replacement, deployment-surge and load-shedding envelope.
Customer/provider responsibility matrix for IaaS, managed data and serverless choices.
AWS, Azure and Google Cloud mechanism translations with current primary-source dates and no false equivalence.
Backup/restore/failover runbook, authority, consistency and user-validation gates.
Cost-per-useful-unit model, uncertainty, risks, ADR and stakeholder explanation.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer supplies unseen workload and changes one requirement after first design.
No cloud account, credentials, CLI session, paid resource, real customer data or external mutation.
Every provider claim cites a current official source, service scope, region/tier limitation and review date.
Calculations expose assumptions and distinguish quota from stock and rate limits.
One rejected hypothesis and one design deliberately rejected on risk or complexity are preserved.
Reviewer observes local model evidence, reasoning, delayed retrieval and exact absence of external state.
